Foodie
FOO-dee
noun (Millennial slang)
A person with an enthusiastic, refined interest in food. The word appeared about 1980 (the restaurant critic Gael Greene is often credited) and was popularized by The Official Foodie Handbook (1984) by Ann Barr and Paul Levy. Millennials made foodie culture mainstream in the 2000s–2010s: food television, celebrity chefs, food trucks, farm-to-table restaurants, and, above all, photographing meals for Instagram ("the camera eats first").

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A foodie loves food, not just to eat it but to seek it out, discuss it, photograph it, and rank it: the new taco truck, the tasting menu, the perfect sourdough. The Christian observation: there is real goodness in this. God made food delicious on purpose; He could have made it merely nourishing. "Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works" (Ecc 9:7). The Lord Jesus’ first miracle provided the best wine at a wedding (Joh 2:10), and He was so often at tables that His enemies called Him a glutton. Scripture is full of feasts, and heaven is pictured as a banquet. Careful cooking and grateful eating honour the Giver. But Scripture also names a danger in exactly this area: the belly as god. Paul wept over those "whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things" (Php 3:19). Gluttony is not only overeating; it is an excessive preoccupation with food, the appetite that rules. Esau sold his birthright for a bowl of stew (Gen 25:33-34). The foodie culture can also be a status game, refined taste as a way of looking down on others. A father teaches his children to love good food, to cook it well, to share it generously, and to thank God for it; and to remember that "Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them" (1Co 6:13), while the bread of life endures for ever.

Webster 1828 Definition

A 1980s coinage made Millennial culture (food TV, Instagram meals) for a food enthusiast; enjoying God’s good food with joy is biblical (Ecc 9:7), but the belly can become a god (Php 3:19).

FOODIE, n. (c. 1980; Millennial mainstream, 2000s–2010s) A person with an enthusiastic and discerning interest in food and eating. Culture: food photography, food trucks, tasting menus, "the camera eats first."

Webster (1828), root food: FOOD, noun [ See Feed .] 1. In a general sense, whatever is eaten by animals for nourishment, and whatever supplies nutriment to plants. 2. Meat; aliment; flesh or vegetables eaten for sustaining human life; victuals; provisions; whatever is or may be eaten for nourishment. Feed me with food convenient for me. Proverbs 30:8 . 3. Whatever supplies nourishment and growth to plants, as water, carbonic acid gas, etc. Manuring substances furnish plants with food 4. Something that sustains, nourishes and augments. […]

Decode for parents: teach the joy of good food and the discipline that keeps appetite from ruling.

Key Scripture

Ecc 9:7 — "Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works."

Joh 2:10 — "And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now."

Php 3:19 — "Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.)"

Gen 25:34 — "Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright."

1Co 6:13 — "Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body."

Modern Corruption

Foodie culture rightly delights in God’s good food, but can make the belly a god and taste a status; Scripture commands joyful eating and warns against appetite that rules.

expand to see more

The corruption is appetite enthroned. When food becomes identity, hobby, social currency, and the main thing one looks forward to, it has moved from gift to god. Esau is the warning: "Thus Esau despised his birthright" (Gen 25:34), trading the eternal for a meal. The foodie culture’s photographs, rankings, and refined contempt for ordinary food can also make the table a place of pride rather than fellowship.

The recovery is grateful, generous eating. Christians should cook well, eat with joy, and set wide tables; hospitality is commanded, and good food is a fine instrument of it. Teach the young to thank God before every meal, to fast sometimes so that appetite stays a servant, and to remember the One who said, "I am the bread of life."

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English foda (food) → food + diminutive -ie → c. 1980 foodie → 1984 Official Foodie Handbook → 2000s–2010s Millennial food culture.
